subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Emily Dickinson's 1890 poem "The Solitary Reader."

A book is but a simple thing,

And yet what peace it brings to me!

In moments of uncertainty it calms my mind,

And when at dusk I seek solitude;

When lamplight flickers on the walls,

And in the distance church bells chime,

As Evening, the gentle host, welcomes all,

I read my verses, and find my time.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To compare the speaker to a welcoming host
choices.B: To portray the speaker's enthusiasm for religious practice
choices.C: To describe the types of literature the speaker prefers to read
choices.D: To convey how engaging with books makes the speaker feel

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it accurately states the main purpose of the text. The text begins by declaring that although a book is "but a simple thing," or seemingly insignificant, reading it brings peace and calms the speaker's mind in "moments of uncertainty." The remainder of the text explores the idea that as evening approaches, reading allows the speaker to "find my time," suggesting contentment and self-discovery. Thus, the main purpose of the text is to convey how engaging with books makes the speaker feel.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. Although the text mentions a host, it neither indicates that the host is reading nor does it compare the host to the speaker.
